prompt: We IPO'd in June 2026 on NYSE with a $450M float and $180M revenue. When does SOX actually bite for us, and do we need the auditor attestation?
assertions: States the IPO transition correctly: the first annual report may omit 404(a) and 404(b); management's first 404(a) ICFR assessment is required in the SECOND Form 10-K; §302/§906 certifications apply immediately

Applies filer logic: $450M float + $180M revenue makes the company an accelerated filer under current thresholds ($75M-$700M float and ≥$100M revenue), so 404(b) auditor attestation applies once transition accommodations and any EGC status end
Checks EGC status: with revenue under $1.235B the company is likely an EGC (JOBS Act §103) and exempt from 404(b) for up to 5 years post-IPO unless disqualified earlier
Flags the pending May 19, 2026 SEC proposal (large accelerated at $2B float; all non-accelerated exempt from 404(b); ~5-year on-ramp) as NOT FINAL — current thresholds remain operative law
Recommends starting ITGC design in year one anyway (scoping, access/change controls), since remediation windows and auditor reliance need operating history
